'''Boualem Khouider''' is an [[Algerian Canadians|Algerian-Canadian]] applied [[mathematician]], [[Climatology|climate scientist]], academic, and author. He is a professor, and former Chair of Mathematics and Statistics at the [[University of Victoria]].<ref name=ool>{{cite web|url=https://www.uvic.ca/science/math-statistics/people/home/faculty/khouider_boualem.php|title=Boualem Khouider - University of Victoria}}</ref>
 
Khouider has published more than 100 papers with his most recognizable contributions being in the [[applied mathematics]], [[atmospheric science]], as well as climate modelling.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.ca/citations?user=cB3TmusAAAAJ&hl=en|title= Boualem Khouider - Google Scholar Profile}}</ref> He is the author of a book ''Models for Tropical Climate Dynamics: Waves, Clouds, and Precipitation'', and is the editor of several edited volumes. He is also a Senior Fellow of [[Institute for Pure and Applied Mathematics]] (IPAM) at the [[University of California Los Angeles]], a senior advisor of Center for Prototype Climate Models at [[New York University Abu Dhabi|NYU Abu-Dhabi Institute]], and holds editorial appointments as an editor for Mathematics of Climate and Weather Forecasting,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.degruyter.com/view/j/mcwf|title= Mathematics of Climate and Weather Forecasting }}</ref> and as associate editor for AIMS Mathematics,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aimspress.com/news/203.html|title= AIMS Press news}}</ref>

==Education==
Khouider received a "High studies diploma" (DES) in Mathematical Analysis of Partial Differential Equations from the [[University of Science and Technology Houari Boumediene|University of Sciences and Technology Houari Boumedienne]] in 1990. He then enrolled at [[University of Montreal]], and earned his Master's and doctoral degrees in Applied Mathematics in 1997 and 2002, respectively.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=69067|title= Boualem Khouider - The Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref>

==Career==
Khouider began his academic career as an assistant lecturer at [[National Polytechnic School (Algeria)|Ecole Nationale Polytechnique]] in 1990, and was subsequently appointed as an assistant lecturer at the University of Sciences and Technology Houari Boumedienne from 1992 until 1994. During this time period, he also held concurrent appointments as lecturer at [[École navale|Ecole Nationale Naval]], and Institut National de Formation en Batiment. In 1995, he held a brief appointment as lecturer at Ecole Militaire Polytechnique, before being appointed by the University of Montreal as a Teaching Assistant, and by Center of Research on Applied Computations (Cerca) as a research assistant from 1996 to 2000. Following this, he was appointed as a research associate in [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] at [[New York University]] until 2003. He held his next appointment at the University of Victoria as [[Assistant professor|Assistant Professor]] Mathematics and Statistics in 2003, and was promoted to associate professor in 2008, and to Full Professor in 2013.<ref name=ool/>

Khouider's contribution to the community includes his role as an organizer of the conferences and workshops, especially the ones in Banff and Oberwolfach. He has also conducted invited lectures and presentations at various professional institutions, including New York University, DongHua University,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wjbjdsyy.com/3d/72/c18211a212338/page.html|title=Differential Equations and Mathematical Biology}}</ref> and the University of Sciences and Technology Houari Boumedienne.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00162-012-0260-3|title=A numerical investigation of the barotropic instability on the equatorial β-plane|year=2013 |doi=10.1007/s00162-012-0260-3 |last1=Kacimi |first1=Abderrahim |last2=Khouider |first2=Boualem |journal=Theoretical and Computational Fluid Dynamics |volume=27 |issue=3–4 |pages=491–512 |bibcode=2013ThCFD..27..491K |s2cid=253690454 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Research==
Khouider's work mainly focuses on applied mathematics, in particular in the fields of [[computational fluid dynamics]], earth System modelling, sea-ice dynamics modelling, tropical meteorology, tropical extra-tropical interactions, organized convection and convectively coupled waves. His research work has been supported by numerous professional organizations, including Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council (NSERC), Canadian Foundation for Climate and Atmospheric Research, [[Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology]], and Pacific Institute for Mathematical Sciences.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Boualem-Khouider|title= Boualem Khouider – ResearchGate Profile}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uvic.ca/science/assets/docs/science-matters/ScienceMattersFall2012.pdf|title=Science Matters}}</ref>

===Atmospheric science===
Khouider conducted a detailed dynamical analysis for the linear waves in 2006, while developing a systematic model convective parameterization focused on highlighting the dynamic role of the three cloud types, congestus, stratiform, and deep convective cumulus clouds, in terms of exploring the dynamics of large-scale convectively coupled Kelvin waves, westward-propagating two-day waves, and the Madden–Julian oscillation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/atsc/63/4/jas3677.1.xml|title= A Simple Multicloud Parameterization for Convectively Coupled Tropical Waves. Part I: Linear Analysis }}</ref> In a companion paper, he presented a report on idealized nonlinear numerical simulations in the context of the developed model.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/atsc/64/2/jas3833.1.xml|title= A Simple Multicloud Parameterization for Convectively Coupled Tropical Waves. Part II: Nonlinear Simulations }}</ref> Furthermore, he highlighted how the adequate representation of the dominant intraseasonal and synoptic-scale variability in the tropics, characterized by the Madden–Julian oscillation (MJO) and convectively coupled waves, continues to be a problem in current operational general circulation models (GCMs).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/atsc/68/2/2010jas3443.1.xml|title= The MJO and Convectively Coupled Waves in a Coarse-Resolution GCM with a Simple Multicloud Parameterization }}</ref>

Khouider discussed the role of environmental moisture in terms of the deepening of cumulus convection. It was found out that the mixing of water vapor by subgrid-scale turbulence has a significant impact on cloud depth, while the mixing of sensible heat has comparatively a negligible impact.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/atsc/67/8/2010jas3357.1.xml|title= The Deepening of Tropical Convection by Congestus Preconditioning }}</ref> In another study, he presented a paradigm model, and provided the applications of the stochastic multicloud framework in terms of improving deterministic parameterizations with clear deficiencies.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/atsc/69/3/jas-d-11-0148.1.xml|title= Using the Stochastic Multicloud Model to Improve Tropical Convective Parameterization: A Paradigm Example }}</ref> Moreover, he along with co-worker, demonstrated the linear stability results for the multicloud model on an equatorial beta plane.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/atsc/65/11/2008jas2752.1.xml|title= Equatorial Convectively Coupled Waves in a Simple Multicloud Model }}</ref>

===Climate modelling===
In 2010, Khouider developed a stochastic multicloud model to represent the missing variability that occurred in global climate models due to unresolved features of organized tropical convection. Furthermore, he coupled stochastic multicloud model to a simple tropical climate model consisting of a system of ODEs, and highlighted the dynamical features of the coupled model.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/communications-in-mathematical-sciences/volume-8/issue-1/A-stochastic-multicloud-model-for-tropical-convection/cms/1266935019.full|title=A stochastic multicloud model for tropical convection}}</ref> Using a statistical inference method based on the Bayesian paradigm, he estimated the stochasticity of convection in terms of Giga-LES data.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00382-015-2936-z|title=Stochasticity of convection in Giga-LES data|year=2016 |doi=10.1007/s00382-015-2936-z |last1=de la Chevrotière |first1=Michèle |last2=Khouider |first2=Boualem |last3=Majda |first3=Andrew J. |journal=Climate Dynamics |volume=47 |issue=5–6 |pages=1845–1861 |bibcode=2016ClDy...47.1845D |s2cid=16432457 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> In his study conducted in 2019, he demonstrated the stochastic parametrization of organized convection, and also explored the performance of the stochastic multicloud model in a stand-alone mode where the cloud model is forced directly by the observed predictors without feedback into the environmental variables.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Using Radar Data to Calibrate a Stochastic Parametrization of Organized Convection|year=2019 |doi=10.1029/2018MS001537 |last1=Cardoso-Bihlo |first1=E. |last2=Khouider |first2=B. |last3=Schumacher |first3=C. |last4=de la Chevrotière |first4=M. |journal=Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems |volume=11 |issue=6 |pages=1655–1684 |bibcode=2019JAMES..11.1655C |s2cid=164934729 |doi-access=free }}</ref> Later on, he successfully implemented the stochastic multicloud model in the CFSv2 GCM, used by the Indian Institute for Tropical Meteorology which led to huge improvements of the climate model in terms of simulating tropical modes of variability, including the MJO, monsoon intra-seasonal oscillations, and convectively coupled equatorial waves.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Implementation and calibration of a stochastic multicloud convective parameterization in the NCEP Climate Forecast System (CFSv2)|year=2017 |doi=10.1002/2017MS001014 |last1=Goswami |first1=B. B. |last2=Khouider |first2=B. |last3=Phani |first3=R. |last4=Mukhopadhyay |first4=P. |last5=Majda |first5=A. J. |journal=Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems |volume=9 |issue=3 |pages=1721–1739 |bibcode=2017JAMES...9.1721G |s2cid=35916073 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/atsc/74/10/jas-d-17-0113.1.xml|title=Improved Tropical Modes of Variability in the NCEP Climate Forecast System (Version 2) via a Stochastic Multicloud Model}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Improving synoptic and intraseasonal variability in CFSv2 via stochastic representation of organized convection|year=2017 |doi=10.1002/2016GL071542 |last1=Goswami |first1=B. B. |last2=Khouider |first2=B. |last3=Phani |first3=R. |last4=Mukhopadhyay |first4=P. |last5=Majda |first5=A. |journal=Geophysical Research Letters |volume=44 |issue=2 |pages=1104–1113 |bibcode=2017GeoRL..44.1104G |s2cid=18523216 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Khouider also proposed a non-oscillatory balanced numerical scheme with application to preserve geostrophic steady states with minimal ad hoc dissipation by using state of the art numerical methods for each piece.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00162-005-0170-8?error=cookies_not_supported&code=aea091ea-2f30-463e-b517-29682cb5a18d|title= A non-oscillatory balanced scheme for an idealized tropical climate model |year= 2005 |doi= 10.1007/s00162-005-0170-8 |last1= Khouider |first1= Boualem |last2= Majda |first2= Andrew J. |journal= Theoretical and Computational Fluid Dynamics |volume= 19 |issue= 5 |pages= 331–354 |s2cid= 8521381 |url-access= subscription }}</ref> Furthermore, he explored and highlighted the role of stratiform heating in the context of scale-selection of organized tropical convection over the monsoon trough, while using aquaplanet version of a coarse-resolution atmospheric [[general circulation model]] coupled to a stochastic multicloud cumulus parameterization scheme.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00382-016-3033-7?error=cookies_not_supported&code=3b627580-d618-4131-b04f-75c3144ec77c|title= Role of stratiform heating on the organization of convection over the monsoon trough |year= 2016 |doi= 10.1007/s00382-016-3033-7 |last1= Ajayamohan |first1= R. S. |last2= Khouider |first2= Boualem |last3= Majda |first3= Andrew J. |last4= Deng |first4= Qiang |journal= Climate Dynamics |volume= 47 |issue= 12 |pages= 3641–3660 |bibcode= 2016ClDy...47.3641A |s2cid= 46459202 |url-access= subscription }}</ref>  In his paper titled "Climate science in the tropics: waves, vortices and PDEs," he presented a review on the interdisciplinary contributions over the last decade through the modus operandi of applied mathematics to most frequently occurring scientific problems. He discussed novel multiscale equations, PDEs, and numerical algorithms with the purpose to persuade mathematicians and physicists to do research in this particular area of study.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0951-7715/26/1/R1/meta|title=Climate science in the tropics: waves, vortices and PDEs |year=2013 |doi=10.1088/0951-7715/26/1/R1 |last1=Khouider |first1=Boualem |last2=Majda |first2=Andrew J. |last3=Stechmann |first3=Samuel N. |journal=Nonlinearity |volume=26 |issue=1 |pages=R1–R68 |bibcode=2013Nonli..26R...1K |s2cid=11599700 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> In a recent study, he conducted a comparative analysis between four theories of the Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO), which lead to a realization that theoretical thinking of the MJO is diverse and understanding of MJO dynamics needs to be further advanced.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Four Theories of the Madden-Julian Oscillation|year=2020 |doi=10.1029/2019RG000685 |last1=Zhang |first1=C. |last2=Adames |first2=Á. F. |last3=Khouider |first3=B. |last4=Wang |first4=B. |last5=Yang |first5=D. |journal=Reviews of Geophysics |volume=58 |issue=3 |article-number=e2019RG000685 |pmid=32879923 |pmc=7375192 |bibcode=2020RvGeo..5800685Z |s2cid=219012061 }}</ref>
